questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I just really like Paris.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was challenging to find the right information from Sorbonne especially concerning the inscription process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a information meeting in the beginning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at the CIUP (Cite Internationale Universitaire Paris) and can really recommend that. I applied through the Danish house (Fondation Danoise). It is quite cheap (compared Parisian standarts) and easy to get a place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The inscription process was quite confusing and stressing. The course inscription in my UFR (institute) was done with pen on paper the week before the start of the courses but if you had to take courses at the other UFR's the inscription was online and it was difficult for the administrative people to coordinate the two.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There wasn't much help - my coordinator got very annoyed when I wrote and asked her questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Accept that it is stressful and chaotic - everything is going to work out in the end even though it might not seem like it. And ask the other exchange students for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the academic level of the courses was a lot lower than at UCPH - we did not read theoretic or secondary literature only literary works (I study comparative literature). The courses I had in English were especially "easy", they had the level of Danish high school courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a lot different. The purpose of the courses seemed to be to memorize what the teacher said so that you could repeat it in your exam. All exams were pen on paper.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Littérature francaise du XIX et XX siecles
Etudes comparatistes
American fiction
British history from 1914-2010
American history in the first half of the 20th century

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think the courses change each semester. If you study literature then I recommend you look at what books you have to read for the courses before you choose - then you can choose based on what books you would like to read.

questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books are very cheap, public transportation is quite expensive. You can eat super cheap at Crous which is a student's cantine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of activities were available at Sorbonne but I didn't use any. At CIUP I joined the sports programme.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is cheap and easy to visit other french cities by train. The trains are very fast so you can get to fx Bordeaux in two hours. There are also lots of fun things to do in Paris of course. Most museums are free if you're under 26.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy - not that far from Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is very difficult. It seems like the French students are not interested in becoming friends with exchange students and since there is no group work in the classes it is difficult to meet people. If you are single then I think dating is the easiest way to meet french people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Parisians can be quite rude and angry, you have to get used to that and remember that it is not personal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and architecture - and that people engage with strangers much more than in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Embrace the administrative chaos - it is going to work out in the end.
Take courses in French even if you don't speak it perfectly (if you want to improve) - the teachers are kind to exchange students when grading.
Find friends who are also exchange students - otherwise you will be lonely.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends and improving my French.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The pen on paper exams in French. I was very nervous but it went just fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
